result.response:
The bug and its cause have been identified and resolved.

### Root Cause
In [`Lexer.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_a_blind/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/csv/Lexer.java#L87-L115), the `readEscape()` method unconditionally returned the character `c` in the `default` branch for characters that were not standard escape characters (`\r`, `\n`, `\t`, `\b`, `\f`). Consequently, non-special escaped characters (such as `\a`, `\N`, or `/` in `/"`) had their escape character stripped instead of signalling to [`CSVLexer`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_a_blind/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVLexer.java#L163-L168) that an unexpected escaped character was read.

### Fix
In [`Lexer.readEscape`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_a_blind/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/csv/Lexer.java#L109-L115), the `default` branch now checks whether `c` is a format meta-character (`delimiter`, `escape`, `quoteChar`, or `commentStart`) and returns `c` if so; otherwise, it returns `END_OF_STREAM`. This allows [`CSVLexer`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_a_blind/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVLexer.java) to append both the escape character and the subsequent character.

### Verification
All previously failing tests pass:
- `org.apache.commons.csv.CSVLexerTest::testEscapedMySqlNullValue`
- `org.apache.commons.csv.CSVLexerTest::testEscapedCharacter`
- `org.apache.commons.csv.CSVParserTest::testBackslashEscaping`

The patch has been saved to [blind_fix.patch](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_a_blind/blind_fix.patch).
